_comment: THE QUALITY BAR AS CODE — the single source of truth for every deployment gate
in this repo.
WHO READS THIS FILE
cert_common.agent_gate_thresholds(use_case) and agent_advisory_thresholds()
-> agents/*.py register_agent(), which run_usecase_certification.py turns
into one avg-score evaluator per dimension plus a usecase_certification_gate.
cert_common.model_gate_threshold() supplies run_certification.py's
--threshold default.
tests/test_gate_thresholds.py fails if the registry and this file diverge.
REQUIRED vs ADVISORY BARS
A bare number is a REQUIRED bar. The verdict is all() over the required bars,
so any one of them below its threshold fails the run and the --ci exit code.
{"threshold": 0.70, "required": false} is an ADVISORY bar: it is measured
(an avg_<dim> score), reported in certification_result's comment and in the
runner summary, and recorded in run metadata as advisory_thresholds, but it
never fails a run. Required bars are recorded as gate_thresholds, so the
portal's verdict replay never sees an advisory bar. Use advisory for signals
worth watching on every run that should not block a release on their own:
heuristics, or a new evaluator still being calibrated. advisory-draft's
completeness is advisory for that reason: it is a length and structure
heuristic, not a correctness or safety property. Moving a bar from required
to advisory loosens the gate, so review it like deleting one.
WHY IT IS A FILE AND NOT A PYTHON DICT
This is the artifact to show someone who asks 'what stops a bad prompt or a
worse model reaching production?'. The answer should be a reviewable file in
git — where loosening a bar shows up as a diff in a pull request — not a
constant buried in an agent module, and not a person remembering to check a
dashboard.
HARD BARS vs LOOSE BARS — the split is deliberate
1.00 (hard): regulatory_compliance, and tool_use_correctness where a tool IS
the control. A prohibited phrase in client-facing output, or a compliance
self-check that did not run, is a DEFECT — not a budget to spend. Zero margin
means one genuinely bad item turns the gate red, which is the point.
0.80 (loose): groundedness, the only LLM-as-a-judge dimension gated here.
Judges carry run-to-run noise on an unchanged input, so a tight judge bar
buys flaky gates and can block a correct fix on a bad roll. Treat it as a
smoke alarm for a catastrophic drop, not a ruler for two-point differences.
0.85-0.90 (calibrated): the correctness dimensions (numerical_accuracy,
sentiment_accuracy) and tool_use_correctness on 10k-analyst, which is 0.90
rather than 1.00 because the calculator is only expected on the subset of
FinanceBench items whose question_reasoning is numerical.
HONEST GAP — THESE NUMBERS ARE NOT VARIANCE-TESTED
They are reasoned from what each dimension measures, not derived from repeat
runs. Nothing here has been run twice on an unchanged target to establish how
much a mean moves on its own, so the calibrated bars above could be sitting
inside their own noise band. Before leaning on a near-miss as a signal, run
the same gate twice against the same model and prompt and record both means
in this comment. A same-target swing larger than a target-to-target delta
means the dimension cannot tell those targets apart, and the bar should be
loosened to smoke-alarm duty like groundedness.
KNOWN GAP — WHAT NO BAR HERE COVERS
exact_match is deliberately absent from 10k-analyst: strict string
containment is near-useless for derived numerical answers (it scored ~40%
while the gate passed, which reads as a broken gate rather than a strict
one). numerical_accuracy covers correctness and groundedness covers
faithfulness. But no bar here covers persona, tone, or brand voice, so a
regression in how an answer reads cannot fail these gates. That is the nature
of a gate: it enforces the dimensions you chose to define and is silent about
the rest. Closing it needs a NUMERIC persona score added to the item
evaluators and a bar for it here.
DATASET ROUTING IS NOT ARBITRARY
advisory-draft is gated on certification/advisory-adversarial, never on
financebench. FinanceBench items carry question_reasoning='Numerical
reasoning', which makes tool_use_correctness demand the calculator tool that
agent never uses — so its hard 1.00 bar can never pass there. The routing
lives in scripts/recert_for_prompt.py and the Makefile's agent-gate target.
DO NOT DELETE AN ENTRY TO SILENCE A FAILING DIMENSION
usecase_certification_gate is all() over the required dimensions it is
given, and all() over an empty dict is True — an agent registered with no
required thresholds would certify PASSED unconditionally, whatever its
advisory bars say. cert_common raises at import on a missing or empty entry,
and on an entry whose bars are all advisory, for exactly this reason.
Removing a bar is how a gate silently stops being one.
